description: Conversion of house (Class C3) into Care Home (Class C2) for 6 number of adults (additional information received 19.05.25)
decision_conditions: The application fails to adequately demonstrate that the proposed care home use does not result in an overconcentration of similar uses in the immediate area and could not be achieved through use of existing sites. Furthermore, the proposal does not sufficiently show that it would integrate appropriately with the residential character of the locality, including safeguarding local amenity. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policies DMH 8 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy H12 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposal to extend the hardstanding area for additional car parking would result in a significant reduction of soft landscaping to the front garden. The increased hardstanding would detract from the visual amenity and character of the site and the wider streetscene, contrary to Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policies BE1, DMHB 11, and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan, and guidance in the NPPF (2024).

In the absence of an arboricultural report, the application has not demonstrated that the proposed additional hardstanding would not cause harm to the adjacent tree or how any potential impacts would be mitigated. This failure to provide necessary information means the proposal is contrary to Policy DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan (2020), Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), and the design objectives of the NPPF (2024).

The proposal would result in increased noise and disturbance from additional vehicle movements and comings and goings, which would adversely affect the residential amenities of surrounding occupiers. The application fails to adequately mitigate these impacts, contrary to Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020), and Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
